Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording

11

“she intended him, and he intended her”

Four explanations transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid ibn Jabr and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr (Q 12:24).

394
Explanation from Ibn ʿAbbās No. 394: 14: 5

Ibn ʿAbbās

English
Transmission wording
394: 14:5. Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj and Salim, or one of them, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, from Ibn Abbas, on His words
"she intended him, and he intended her": He said, she yielded to him, and his drawers were loosened, and he sat between her thighs. Then a caller called, "Joseph, do not be like the bird which, when it drew near, lost its feathers." He took no heed of the call at all. He was called a second time and took no heed of the call at all. Then Jacob appeared to him and struck his chest. He stood up, and the desire went out through his fingertips (verse 24).
العربية
394: 14: 5 سفيان عن بن جُرَيْجٍ وَسَالِمٍ أَوْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَنِ بن أبي مليكة عن بن عباس في قوله همت به وهم بها قَالَ أَسْلَمَتْ لَهُ وَحَلَّ التَّبَانُ وَقَعَدَ بَيْنَ فَخِذَيْهَا فَنَادَى مُنَادٍ يا يوسف لا تكن كالطاير قال إِذَا دَمَا ذَهَبَ رِيشُهُ فَلَمْ يعظ عن الندا شيا فَنُودِيَ الثَّانِيَةَ فَلَمْ يَعِظْ عَنِ الندا شيا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهُ يَعْقُوبُ فَضَرَبَ صَدْرَهُ فَقَامَ فَخَرَجَتِ الشَّهْوَةُ مِنْ أَنَامِلِهِ (الآية 24) .
